title: Microsoft Purview: DLP for network traffic through Entra Global Secure Access Internet Access
summary: Hold: the Purview configuration path skips the required Custom and Custom policy choices in the policy wizard. The licensing differences, default state, rollout dates and documented inspection limitations are accurately attributed to their sources.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Purview DLP integrates with Entra Global Secure Access Internet Access to inspect sensitive files and text sent to unmanaged cloud and AI apps across browsers and applications.
claims.quote: These controls apply to content shared from managed endpoints through browsers, applications, add-ins, APIs, and more. ... It inspects files and text for sensitive information and helps prevent data loss by blocking its sharing based on your Purview DLP policies.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Scan with Purview requires a matching Purview DLP policy targeting inline web traffic to inspect content or enforce audit or block decisions.
claims.quote: Without a matching Purview DLP policy, the content policy can't inspect selected file or text content or enforce audit or block decisions.

claims.claim: The notice lists the integration as altering how existing customer data is processed.
claims.quote:
Alters how existing customer data is processed
Sensitive file traffic is inspected at the network layer before reaching unmanaged cloud apps.

claims.claim: The documented maximum inspected file size is 3 MB.
claims.quote: Inline evaluation size limits: Microsoft Purview evaluates up to 4 MB of content for uploadText and downloadText, and files up to 3 MB for uploadFile and downloadFile.

claims.claim: OCR is not yet supported for traffic sent to Purview.
claims.quote: OCR is not yet supported for traffic sent to Purview.

claims.claim: Files encoded within JSON may escape inspection.
claims.quote: Certain file transfer methods may prevent inspection, such as if an application encodes a file within a JSON, or the file is broken up into multiple encrypted requests.

claims.claim: Files split across multiple encrypted requests may escape inspection.
claims.quote: Certain file transfer methods may prevent inspection, such as if an application encodes a file within a JSON, or the file is broken up into multiple encrypted requests.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The content policy page states a 3 MB maximum for text, in contrast with the other cited page.
claims.quote: The maximum supported content size for Scan with Purview is 3 MB for both file and text content types.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The network data security page states a 4 MB inline text evaluation limit.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview evaluates up to 4 MB of content for uploadText and downloadText

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Traffic is allowed fail-open when Purview inspection cannot complete, including oversized payloads or internal errors.
claims.quote: In scenarios where Purview inspection is unable to complete, such as a payload that is too large to inspect, or an internal error, the traffic is allowed (fail-open).

claims.claim: The PurviewStatus field in traffic logs identifies transactions that skipped inspection.
claims.quote: Transactions that have skipped inspection can be identified in Traffic logs using PurviewStatus field.

claims.claim: Scan with Purview applies only to traffic associated with an Entra user identity.
claims.quote: Scan with Purview only applies to traffic associated with an Entra user identity.

claims.claim: Purview network data security policies do not apply to B2B guest users.
claims.quote: Purview network data security policies don't apply to B2B guest users.

claims.claim: Traffic that cannot be mapped to an Entra user identity is not sent to Purview for inspection.
claims.quote: Traffic that cannot be mapped to an Entra user identity is not sent to Purview for inspection.

claims.claim: TLS inspection policy configuration is a prerequisite.
claims.quote: Configure the Transport Layer Security (TLS) inspection policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn requires installing and configuring the Global Secure Access client on Windows or macOS.
claims.quote:
Install and configure the Global Secure Access client:
1. Install the Global Secure Access client on Windows or macOS.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Global Secure Access client requires a device that is Entra ID joined or hybrid joined.
claims.quote: The Global Secure Access client requires a device (or virtual machine) that is either Microsoft Entra ID joined or Microsoft Entra ID Hybrid joined.

claims.claim: UDP traffic, including QUIC, is not supported.
claims.quote: User Datagram Protocol (UDP) traffic (that is, QUIC) isn't supported.

claims.claim: Sites that support fallback can use TCP when QUIC cannot be established.
claims.quote: Most websites support fallback to Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) when QUIC can't be established.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The Block action can stop matched text submissions or file uploads.
claims.quote: Test the configuration by attempting to upload or download files, or send text content, that matches the content policy conditions. Verify that the policy settings audit or block the actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The DLP policy can run in simulation mode before being turned on.
claims.quote: On the Policy mode page, choose Turn the policy on immediately or run in simulation mode first to test.

claims.claim: Learn's ChatGPT test shows an error when Global Secure Access blocks a file upload.
claims.quote: Verify that the upload is blocked. ChatGPT displays an error message because Global Secure Access prevented the file transfer.

claims.claim: Blocking HTML or JSON text types in basic content rules can unintentionally block normal web and API traffic.
claims.quote: Web requests and responses commonly use HTML or JSON payloads, so blocking these text types can unintentionally block normal web and API traffic, including GET, POST, and PUT operations.

claims.claim: Requests are subject to API rate limiting.
claims.quote: Requests are subject to API rate limiting based on usage.

claims.claim: Traffic is blocked fail-closed when rate limits are exceeded.
claims.quote: When limits are exceeded, traffic is automatically blocked (fail-closed).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Purview rule actions should match the content policy's activities and content types.
claims.quote: The actions you select in the Purview DLP rule should match the content types and activities you selected in the Global Secure Access content policy.

claims.claim: Policy distribution to the network solution can take up to 24 hours after integration is configured.
claims.quote: After you configure the integration between Microsoft Purview and your network security solution, allow up to 24 hours for your policies to be distributed to the network security solution and for the first data to show up.

claims.claim: Data about a request can take up to 30 minutes to appear in the audit log and activity explorer after communication is established.
claims.quote: Once the two services fully communicate with each other, it can take up to 30 minutes for data about a request from a client to a website or cloud app to appear in the audit log and activity explorer.

claims.claim: Application-specific destination coverage can depend on the exact upload URLs and related FQDNs.
claims.quote: For application-specific control, you can add the exact URLs and related FQDNs that the app uses. Use browser developer tools or network traffic analysis to identify the endpoints used during file upload, text submission, or other protected traffic.

claims.claim: The Entra path to Scan with Purview is Global Secure Access > Secure > Content policies > + Create Policy > Rules > rule > Action > Scan with Purview.
claims.quote: On the Basics tab: ... Select Next. ... On the Rules tab: ... Add a new rule. ... Select the appropriate option for the Action menu: ... To use data policies configured in Microsoft Purview, select Scan with Purview.
claims.fix: Include the intervening Basics wizard page in both copies of the path: Global Secure Access > Secure > Content policies > + Create Policy > Basics > Rules > rule > Action > Scan with Purview. The cited content-policy page supplies these steps.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Graph operation is documented for setting Scan with Purview in content policy rules at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Global Secure Access content policy rules Scan with Purview Microsoft Graph API contentFilteringRule; "Microsoft Graph" "content policies" "Purview". Read content-policy guide, Graph Internet Access tutorial and beta filteringRule reference; no matching operation.

claims.claim: The printed Purview path reaches the rule action directly from Inline web traffic through Choose where to enforce the policy, without choosing Custom and Custom policy.
claims.quote: Select Inline web traffic. ... Select Custom from the Categories list and then select Custom policy from the Regulations list.
claims.fix: Replace the path in controls[1].ui and its rendered table row with: Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Inline web traffic > Custom > Custom policy > Choose where to enforce the policy > Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > + Create rule > Actions > + Add an action > Restrict browser and network activities. The cited content-policy guide requires the Custom and Custom policy choices and enabling Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers.

claims.claim: An automation operation that configures the inline network DLP rule's audit or block action is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Restrict browser and network activities" "PowerShell"; "network" "DLP" "AdvancedRule" "uploadText". Read New-DlpComplianceRule and New-DlpCompliancePolicy references and network policy guides; no documented network audit/block operation.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy accepts Network for EnforcementPlanes, which selects an enforcement layer rather than a rule's audit or block action.
claims.quote: The EnforcementPlanes parameter defines the layer where policy actions are run. ... Valid values are: ... Network

claims.claim: The beta Graph API is subject to change and production use is not supported.

claims.quote: On the Choose where to enforce the policy page, ensure Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers is enabled ... Under Actions, select + Add an action > Restrict browser and network activities.

claims.claim: Global Secure Access traffic logs provide investigation data for network filtering.
claims.quote: To confirm the block, check the traffic logs in the Microsoft Entra admin center under Global Secure Access > Monitor > Traffic logs.
